messages.author: 1e94001192669559
messages.subject: specifying start values for intercepts.
parts:
Sorry for the newbie question, but I can't seem to locate an answer: I wish to specify a start value for an intercept because the model doesn't otherwise converge. Although I see how to do this for loadings and regression weights, it seems that I must be missing something for intercepts. Here's a code snippet. The bold, underlined line is the problematic one. I've tried duplicating the line, once with start and once with shift to no avail. Can anyone point me to the Fine Manual? thanks! Phil :

FactorMeanShift.model <-'
  
f =~ NA*wisc1 + wisc2 + wisc3 + wisc4
f ~~ 1*f

wisc1 ~~ ve1*wisc1
wisc2 ~~ ve1*wisc2
wisc3 ~~ ve3*wisc3
wisc4 ~~ ve4*wisc4

wisc1 ~ start(-25)*1 shift*1
wisc2 ~ shift*1
wisc3 ~ shift*1
wisc4 ~ shift*1
f ~ FM*1
'

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: specifying start values for intercepts.
parts:
You are correctly declaring the start value separately from the label, but you need to put an "and" sign between them:

wisc1 ~ start(-25)*1 + shift*1

or put them on 2 separate lines:

wisc1 ~ start(-25)*1 
wisc1 ~ shift*1

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: specifying start values for intercepts.
parts:
This should work. But it does not (in 0.5-18). This must be a bug in the
parser. It only happens when you both try to label and provide a
starting value for an intercept ('1'). I will try to fix this asap.

As a workaround, the 'old' way for providing labels still works:

lavaanify('wisc1 ~ start(-25)*1 + label("shift")*1')

(as an aside, this example also illustrates why I always insist that the
model syntax should be between *single* quotes)

Yves.
